groups.text: It is currently 16 degrees and cloudy in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

Chinese developers are systematically bypassing Anthropic's strict access controls to use the AI model Claude. Despite geoblocking, credit card checks, and biometric selfie verification, a thriving gray market has emerged in China. These users buy tokens through "transfer stations" for as little as ten percent of the official list price. These API proxies route requests through overseas servers to hide their origin. Operators lower costs by exploiting free credits or secretly swapping expensive models for cheaper alternatives. Zilan Qian, a researcher at the Oxford China Policy Lab, warns that this modular supply chain does more than just undermine geoblocking. This network weakens Anthropic's ability to monitor misuse and may fuel criminal markets centered on payment and identity fraud. The situation highlights a direct conflict between corporate safety restrictions and the persistence of underground digital trade.

The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine reports that Russia has lost approximately 1,476,580 troops since the full-scale invasion began on February 24, 2022. This total includes 1,310 casualties suffered over the past day alone. The material toll is equally steep, with losses including 12,292 tanks, 25,202 armored combat vehicles, and 48,451 artillery systems. Russia has also lost 474,641 unmanned aerial vehicles, 5,052 cruise missiles, and two submarines. Ukraine maintains operational secrecy regarding its own losses, but the Center for Strategic and International Studies estimates a casualty ratio of roughly 2.5 to 1 or 2 to 1 in favor of Ukraine. In a report from January 2026, that think-tank estimated Ukrainian casualties between February 2022 and December 2025 were likely between 500,000 and 600,000 people, with 100,000 to 140,000 of those killed in action.

The Eisenbahn- und Verkehrsgewerkschaft union is threatening a nationwide strike across Germany's regional rail network starting in January. Union chief Martin Burkert says the action will happen if the government fails to pass a law introducing harsher penalties for attacks on train staff by the end of this year. This tension follows a brutal incident in February where 36-year-old conductor Serkan Çalar was attacked and killed by a passenger on a regional express in Rheinland-Pfalz. While the attacker was sentenced to ten years in prison for manslaughter in July, Burkert argues that the federal government has offered only empty promises and words instead of legislative action. He claims politicians have forgotten the victim while rail workers continue to risk their health and lives. The union warns that without a concrete legal change in the Bundestag, they will paralyze rail operations.

The Indian Coast Guard is searching for 22 crew members after the Panama-flagged cargo ship Ocean Winner sank in the Bay of Bengal on Friday. The vessel was carrying iron ore from India to Singapore when it began tilting and sank within eight minutes. While two Chinese nationals were rescued Saturday, 18 Chinese, three Myanmar, and one Bangladeshi sailors remain missing. In a separate tragedy near Middlesbrough, a wrong-way crash on the A66 killed two Cleveland Police officers, PC Matthew Blades and PC Tom Clough, along with five people in their late teens or early twenties. The Independent Office for Police Conduct is now investigating the collision between the police vehicle and a Volkswagen Passat. Meanwhile, organizers of the Sydney Marathon are dealing with a mistake on the medals for 40,000 expected runners. Instead of Sydney's Allianz Stadium, the medals were minted with an image of the Allianz Arena in Munich, Germany.

A trade war has erupted between the United States and Canada after negotiations in Washington collapsed on Friday. The conflict began when the U.S. imposed fifty percent tariffs on a broad range of Canadian products, including cement and hockey sticks, affecting roughly twenty billion dollars in goods. Prime Minister Mark Carney responded Saturday by announcing that Canada will match these tariffs dollar for dollar to protect its workers and businesses. These retaliatory measures specifically target the U.S. dairy and steel industries and will take effect on September 8. President Donald Trump hit back on Sunday via Truth Social, accusing Canada of wanting the benefits of being a U.S. state without actually being one. He further claimed that Canada has unfairly charged American farmers massive amounts in tariffs for many years and declared that those practices must end.

Trade tensions are escalating between the United States and Canada after Donald Trump imposed fifty percent tariffs on Canadian products this Saturday. In response, Prime Minister Mark Carney announced retaliatory tariffs targeting American steel and dairy products. President Trump responded Sunday, claiming Canada wants the advantages of being a U.S. state without actually being one, and he has threatened to further increase those tariffs. Meanwhile, in Ukraine, former defense minister Mykhailo Fedorov released a video on August 18 criticizing a systemic crisis of governance and corruption. Fedorov also highlighted that no national elections have been held since 2019. These remarks came just as President Volodymyr Zelenskyy proposed Yevhenii Khmara for the defense ministry, who was confirmed by parliament on August 19. The day after Fedorov's speech, anti-corruption investigators searched the premises of several high-ranking officials, including presidential deputy chief of staff Iryna Mudra.

Australia has confirmed its first case of H5N1 bird flu in a mammal after finding the deadly virus in a long-nosed fur seal. The animal was found dead in the coastal town of Beachport, South Australia, with no signs of injury. Federal Agriculture Minister Julie Collins described the development as concerning but not unexpected, noting that infection in marine mammals is likely where wild bird infection rates are high. Australia has been combating the virus since June and recently reported its first mass seabird deaths; however, officials say the virus has not spread to poultry or agriculture. In sports, Australia bounced back from a shock defeat last week to beat Bangladesh by an innings and 51 runs in the second Test at the Great Barrier Reef Arena in Mackay. Mitchell Starc led the victory with ten wickets in the match, helping Australia draw the series one-to-one.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be cloudy with temperatures between 18 and 20 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.
On your calendar today: Your personal calendar has the Berlin summer holidays and Uschi Bekaan's birthday. Later, you have an appointment with Kierán Braukunst at two in the afternoon.
Mail worth checking: You have a message from Kleinanzeigen regarding your wooden pallets listing, and an invite from info about the Linux Stammtisch this Tuesday.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
